newsitem.title: USA: Fedex aims to be fast - and fashionable.
newsitem.headline: Fedex aims to be fast - and fashionable.

text.p: Stand aside, United Parcel Service couriers with your fetching brown uniforms. Federal Express Corp is upping the ante in the overnight delivery fashion wars, unveiling a new uniform Thursday that its designer calls "more daring."
"There is a more daring use of color, logo and striping in the new uniform. It is more active," said Stan Herman, the designer and a three-time Coty Award winner.

It is also less formal. Herman said he ditched the blazers and vests in favor of softer sweaters and knit shirts. Female employees will be discouraged from wearing skirts in favor of shorts and slacks.
Herman retained the basic "FedEx navy" but is adding "bigger strokes" of orange and purple. Employees will be offered a wide variety of pieces to mix and match.
The new uniforms will be worn by all couriers, ground operators and service center agents or about 73 percent of FedEx's 124,000 employees throughout the world.
The new look will begin appearing next week and all employees will be decked out in the new clothes by December 1997.
UPS and its uniforms won worldwide attention last year following published reports about how some women customers found their brown shorts and clunky shoes sexy.
Although he is not one to dump on the competition, Herman boasted that FedEx delivery people will "look more current" than their UPS rivals.
